8.0.s.en: 1. Esther and the house of Haman:

8.0.0.en: 1 On that day did the king Ahasuerus give the house of Haman the Jews' enemy unto Esther the queen. And Mordecai came before the king; for Esther had told what he was unto her.

8.0.1.en: "On that day did the king Ahasuerus give the house of Haman the Jews' enemy unto Esther the queen" [1].

8.0.2.en: Haman had asked his helpers to cast lots to determine a day on which Haman would inherit all that belonged to the Jews after killing them, yet behold, Haman was delivered to death, and the king gave his house into the hands of Esther the Jewess.

8.0.3.en: If the true Haman, the devil, set in his heart to seize the heart of man and inherit it after crushing and destroying it, then through the banquet of the Cross man took the position that Satan held before his fall, and became as one who has entered into the heavenly orders as one of them. Some of the Fathers see that the heavenly orders are seven, besides the Cherubim and Seraphim, and man has become like the tenth order in place of the devil, who was the morning star standing in the presence of God. The enemy fell into the abyss so that man might rise, be lifted up to heaven and reign in the place of the fallen enemy!

8.0.4.en: If Satan set himself up as the ruler of this world by the enticements of sin (Jn 12:31), seizing the house of man which God gave us to dwell in with authority, then through the banquet of the Cross man not only recovered his house but was raised with the Lord to Paradise. In this connection St. Gregory of Nyssa addresses the candidates for baptism, saying: [You are outside Paradise, O catechumens. You share with Adam your first father in his exile. But now the door is opened and you return to where you came out].

8.0.5.en: The feast of Purim is the feast of the annulment of Haman's lot for the destruction of the believers, so that the Lord may declare that they are His portion, heirs of the house of the fallen enemy, and enjoying entrance into heaven itself.

8.1.0.en: 2 And the king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it unto Mordecai. And Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.

8.1.1.en: "And the king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it unto Mordecai" [2].

8.1.2.en: When the prodigal son returned to his father, the father said: "Put a ring on his hand" (Lk 15:22), a sign of true sonship and a confirmation of his filial authority. So the believer, Mordecai, enjoys the king's ring, as the Evangelist says: "As many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name: which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God" (Jn 1:12-13). This is the royal ring, the "filial authority" which we receive by the Holy Spirit in the waters of Baptism. For this reason many Fathers spoke of Baptism as a seal on the soul, such as St. Clement of Rome, Hermas, Tertullian and St. John Chrysostom. St. Augustine says of this seal: [Hold fast to what you have received, for it will not change; it is a royal mark]. By this seal we enter into the possession of God, as the Father Theodore of Mopsuestia says: [The sign with which you are now marked is a sign that you have become the flock of Christ]. By this seal we also enter into spiritual soldiery, and as St. Cyril of Jerusalem says: [Each one of you comes and presents himself before God, in the presence of countless armies of angels, and the Holy Spirit sets a mark upon your souls. By this you enroll yourselves in the army of the great King].

8.1.3.en: By this seal, as we enjoy the authority of sonship and live in the possession of God as His children, and live as spiritual strugglers, as His soldiers, we enjoy the eternal feast, inheriting the glory that does not perish. As the Apostle says: "The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: and if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ" (Rom 8:16-17).

8.2.0.en: 3 And Esther spake yet again before the king, and fell down at his feet, and besought him with tears to put away the mischief of Haman the Agagite, and his device that he had devised against the Jews. 4 Then the king held out the golden sceptre toward Esther. So Esther arose, and stood before the king. If Mordecai received the king's seal as a sign of enjoying the eternal feast, then Esther enjoyed appearing before the king; this appearing in his presence is the true "feast", where the Church enjoys the companionship of God, His dwelling within her, and her entrance into His bosom.

8.2.1.en: The Scripture says: "And Esther spake yet again before the king, and fell down at his feet, and besought him with tears to put away the mischief of Haman the Agagite, and his device that he had devised against the Jews. Then the king held out the golden sceptre toward Esther. So Esther arose, and stood before the king" [3-4].

8.2.2.en: The true feast is a meeting with the Lord or a standing before Him; it is a rising after a fall, as the Scripture says of Esther: "fell down at his feet... Then the king held out the golden sceptre toward Esther. So Esther arose...". In other words, the feast is an entrance into the experience of the Resurrection through the Cross (the golden scepter).

8.2.3.en: May we go with Esther to the King, and in contrition declare our fall at His feet, that we may weep with her and plead because of the bitterness of the devil's schemes against us, so that the Lord may stretch out His hand through His heavenly, life-giving Cross, and we may rise and be found with Him eternally.

8.3.s.en: 4. The issuing of the new royal decree:

8.3.0.en: 5 And said, If it please the king, and if I have found favour in his sight, and the thing seem right before the king, and I be pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to reverse the letters devised by Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews which are in all the king's provinces: 6 For how can I endure to see the evil that shall come unto my people? or how can I endure to see the destruction of my kindred? 7 Then the king Ahasuerus said unto Esther the queen and to Mordecai the Jew, Behold, I have given Esther the house of Haman, and him they have hanged upon the gallows, because he laid his hand upon the Jews. 8 Write ye also for the Jews, as it liketh you, in the king's name, and seal it with the king's ring: for the writing which is written in the king's name, and sealed with the king's ring, may no man reverse. 9 Then were the king's scribes called at that time in the third month, that is, the month Sivan, on the three and twentieth day thereof; and it was written according to all that Mordecai commanded unto the Jews, and to the lieutenants, and the deputies and rulers of the provinces which are from India unto Ethiopia, an hundred twenty and seven provinces, unto every province according to the writing thereof, and unto every people after their language, and to the Jews according to their writing, and according to their language. 10 And he wrote in the king Ahasuerus' name, and sealed it with the king's ring, and sent letters by posts on horseback, and riders on mules, camels, and young dromedaries: 11 Wherein the king granted the Jews which were in every city to gather themselves together, and to stand for their life, to destroy, to slay, and to cause to perish, all the power of the people and province that would assault them, both little ones and women, and to take the spoil of them for a prey, 12 Upon one day in all the provinces of king Ahasuerus, namely, upon the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar. 13 The copy of the writing for a commandment to be given in every province was published unto all people, and that the Jews should be ready against that day to avenge themselves on their enemies. 14 So the posts that rode upon mules and camels went out, being hastened and pressed on by the king's commandment. And the decree was given at Shushan the palace.

8.3.1.en: Through Haman the first decree was issued, in which was the sentence of death; and now through Mordecai and Esther, through Esther's banquet, that is, the banquet of the Cross, the first decree was torn up (Col 2:15) and a new decree was issued on our behalf, in which our sonship to God and the destruction of our enemies (the devil and his hosts) are proclaimed.

8.4.0.en: How beautiful are the words of Esther (the Church) to the king as she intercedes for her people: "For how can I endure to see the evil that shall come unto my people? or how can I endure to see the destruction of my kindred?" [6]. These are the feelings of the Church toward every soul, the feelings of shepherds and flock alike, for all are aflame with the love of the salvation of others. These feelings took shape in the words of St. John Chrysostom, who never ceased to pray and labor for the salvation of every soul. Among his words: [Nothing is dearer to me than you, no, not even the light! I would gladly give my eyes tens of thousands of times and more, if possible, for the repentance of your souls. Your salvation is very dear to me, more than the light itself...! For what good are the rays of the sun to me if sorrow darkens my eyes because of you...?! What hope will I have if you do not progress?! And on the contrary, what despair can enter me as long as you are growing?! For when I hear joyful news about you I seem to have grown wings... You wipe away my sorrow! This is the whole burden of my prayers: I long for your growth... I love you, to the point of melting into you, and you are everything to me, my father and my mother, my brothers and my children].

8.4.1.en: Through this love which Mordecai and Esther showed, the new royal decree was issued, and its text is given in the Additions to Esther (Add. Esth 16), in which we find:

8.4.2.en: First: the condemnation of Haman as proud: "Many, the more often they are honored with the great bounty of their gracious princes, the more proud they become" (Add. Esth 16:2). In the former edict Ahasuerus regarded Haman as a father to him, and now he condemns him as proud. So when we fall into sin we regard the enemy as a father, but after the banquet of the Cross his true nature is exposed as a proud creature who abused the gift God gave him.

8.4.3.en: Second: the king reckoned that what had befallen the people had befallen him personally (Add. Esth 16:3-12) and that Haman had wished to deceive the great men and the rulers whom the king had set up. So by the Cross the Lord reckons every attack of the devil upon us and every deception as directed against His own kingdom, touching God Himself because we are His.

8.4.4.en: Third: he called the people: "the children of the most high, the most mighty, the living God, who by His kindness gave the kingdom to our fathers and to us, and has kept it until today" (Add. Esth 16:16). Thus through the events the pagan king touched the hand of God, and the trial became a mystery of blessing, so that many abandoned idolatry and believed in the living God. If the Jews were saved from extermination in the flesh, many of the pagans were saved from the death of idol worship.

8.5.0.en: 15 And Mordecai went out from the presence of the king in royal apparel of blue and white, and with a great crown of gold, and with a garment of fine linen and purple: and the city of Shushan rejoiced and was glad. 16 The Jews had light, and gladness, and joy, and honour. 17 And in every province, and in every city, whithersoever the king's commandment and his decree came, the Jews had joy and gladness, a feast and a good day. And many of the people of the land became Jews; for the fear of the Jews fell upon them.

8.5.1.en: "And Mordecai went out from the presence of the king in royal apparel of blue and white, and with a great crown of gold, and with a garment of fine linen and purple: and the city of Shushan rejoiced and was glad" [15].

8.5.2.en: It would not have been possible for the city of Shushan to put off the garments of mourning and enter into a life of exultation and joy unless Mordecai were first glorified before the king and clothed with the royal apparel, the golden crown and the garment of fine linen and purple. So the Church could not have enjoyed heavenly exultation and spiritual joy unless her Bridegroom, Christ Jesus, were glorified and raised to His Father. As He emptied Himself for our sake, so for our sake He was also glorified, that He might glorify us with Him, and we might put on with Him the royal apparel of blue and white, that is, the heavenly (blue) and pure (white) garment. In Christ Jesus we become kings (Rev 1:6) and put on the heavenly nature filled with purity. Through Him we also enjoy the heavenly (golden) crown, and put on the royal garment of righteousness (fine linen) (purple is the garment of kings).

8.6.0.en: When Mordecai was glorified, "The Jews had light, and gladness, and joy, and honour... And many of the people of the land became Jews; for the fear of the Jews fell upon them" [16-17]. So when the Lord Christ was glorified with the glory that He has from eternity, the Church enjoys light, that is, enlightenment, joy of the Spirit and inward honor...

8.6.1.en: Here, as the Church is glorified by the glorified Christ, we recall the dream that Mordecai saw in the Additions to Esther and its interpretation (Add. Esth 10-11). Mordecai saw voices and tumult, thunders and earthquakes on the earth, and behold, two great dragons were ready to fight, and the nations were stirred up, and the righteous cried out to God, and a little spring grew into a great river and overflowed with many waters, and then was transformed into light and sun. What are these voices but the voices of the Law and the types of the Old Testament that preceded the coming of the Word, to proclaim the spiritual warfare that exists not between Haman and Mordecai (the two great dragons) but between Satan and the Lord Christ; and this little spring, which is Esther, which became great for the people and became light and sun, signifies the Church, which went forth through the Lord Christ, who by His Incarnation humbled Himself and became like a little spring, so that He might overflow upon us with His Holy Spirit and shine in us with the splendor of His divinity, as the light of the world and the Sun of righteousness.

8.6.2.en: The dream carried an interpretation of the events of salvation in the days of Esther, and it carried a symbolic interpretation of the events of the true salvation accomplished by the Lord Christ Himself.

9.0.s.en: 1. The victory and dominion of the Jews:

9.0.0.en: 1 Now in the twelfth month, that is, the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the same, when the king's commandment and his decree drew near to be put in execution, in the day that the enemies of the Jews hoped to have power over them, (though it was turned to the contrary, that the Jews had rule over them that hated them;) 2 The Jews gathered themselves together in their cities throughout all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, to lay hand on such as sought their hurt: and no man could withstand them; for the fear of them fell upon all people. 3 And all the rulers of the provinces, and the lieutenants, and the deputies, and officers of the king, helped the Jews; because the fear of Mordecai fell upon them. 4 For Mordecai was great in the king's house, and his fame went out throughout all the provinces: for this man Mordecai waxed greater and greater. 5 Thus the Jews smote all their enemies with the stroke of the sword, and slaughter, and destruction, and did what they would unto those that hated them. 6 And in Shushan the palace the Jews slew and destroyed five hundred men. 7 And Parshandatha, and Dalphon, and Aspatha, 8 And Poratha, and Adalia, and Aridatha, 9 And Parmashta, and Arisai, and Aridai, and Vajezatha, 10 The ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews, slew they; but on the spoil laid they not their hand.

9.1.0.en: Two royal edicts reached all the provinces. One was sent by Haman from Shushan the palace, dated the thirteenth of the first month, demanding the killing and extermination of the Jews. The second was sent by Mordecai, also from Shushan the palace, dated the twenty-third of the third month, authorizing the Jews to draw the sword against their enemies in defense of themselves. When the thirteenth day of the twelfth month came, the enemies of the Jews resolved to fight them on the basis of the first edict, while the Jews relied on the second edict and rose to fight them, and the Lord gave them awe, for "no man could withstand them; for the fear of them fell upon all people. And all the rulers of the provinces, and the lieutenants, and the deputies, and officers of the king, helped the Jews; because the fear of Mordecai fell upon them" [2-3].

9.1.1.en: Although the enemy (the devil) rages against the Church, yet where he thinks he is able to prevail, he is defeated under her feet, as the Lord Himself says: "the gates of hell shall not prevail against it" (Mt 16:18), and as He says to the Church in Philadelphia: "Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee" (Rev 3:9).

9.2.0.en: Haman prepared the gallows for Mordecai and was hanged on it, and his ten sons were also hanged [14], and since he devised the complete extermination of the people, all his followers perished!

9.2.1.en: The enemies began to oppose the Jews although they knew of the second edict, and wanted to gain dominion over them [1]; they attacked them, and all allied together to harm them [2], and that brought about their own shame. Jewish tradition says that no one stood against this people at that time except the Amalekites, whose hearts were hardened like Pharaoh's, and the sons of Haman were determined to avenge their father's blood at whatever cost.

9.2.2.en: The Scripture says: "The Jews gathered themselves together in their cities throughout all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, to lay hand on such as sought their hurt: and no man could withstand them; for the fear of them fell upon all people" [2].

9.2.3.en: This collective movement carries a spiritual meaning that touches our life in the Lord. The gathering of the Jews in their cities throughout all the provinces of the king signifies the consecration of all the senses of man, his impulses and his energies, each gift in its place, so long as it is in the provinces of the king, that is, subject to the Kingdom of God, so that all of them work together with one spirit and one mind to resist the devil with all his thoughts and enticements, which are an enmity seeking to harm us. Thus no man can withstand us, that is, no sin can have dominion over us so long as all that is in us belongs to the Lord, and we become in the eyes of the devil awesome and terrifying to him.

9.2.4.en: The account continues thus: "And all the rulers of the provinces, and the lieutenants (the stewards), and the deputies, and officers of the king, helped the Jews; because the fear of Mordecai fell upon them" [3].

9.2.5.en: The Jews gathered to act with one spirit and so were terrifying to the enemy, and the officials also supported them because of the awe of Mordecai. I say that this is a picture of spiritual striving. The gathering of the Jews in their cities, as I said, signifies the stirring up of the senses and inward energies for spiritual striving through a life of sanctification, while the rulers, stewards, deputies and officers of the king signify the outward support of man, such as the help of the heavenly orders, the company of the saints who have fallen asleep in the Lord and the prayers of those who are striving... For the person who lives in the Lord carries strength within him and also help through the holy company, whether of those who have fallen asleep or of those who are striving; therefore the Apostle says: "Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us" (Heb 12:1).

9.2.6.en: Since the people carried the power of the Spirit and its unity within, and divine support from without, they struck their enemies... The number of the slain in Shushan the palace reached five hundred men, and the ten sons of Haman were also killed... And the people did not lay their hand on the spoil, although the king had allowed them to do so (Esth 8:11). Perhaps they wanted to confirm their intention before all, that they did not covet material gain nor use the king's edict to achieve private aims, but sought only their deliverance. For this reason also they did not kill the children and women, although they had been permitted to do so (Esth 8:11).

9.3.0.en: 11 On that day the number of those that were slain in Shushan the palace was brought before the king. 12 And the king said unto Esther the queen, The Jews have slain and destroyed five hundred men in Shushan the palace, and the ten sons of Haman; what have they done in the rest of the king's provinces? now what is thy petition? and it shall be granted thee: or what is thy request further? and it shall be done. 13 Then said Esther, If it please the king, let it be granted to the Jews which are in Shushan to do to morrow also according unto this day's decree, and let Haman's ten sons be hanged upon the gallows. 14 And the king commanded it so to be done: and the decree was given at Shushan; and they hanged Haman's ten sons. 15 For the Jews that were in Shushan gathered themselves together on the fourteenth day also of the month Adar, and slew three hundred men at Shushan; but on the prey they laid not their hand. 16 But the other Jews that were in the king's provinces gathered themselves together, and stood for their lives, and had rest from their enemies, and slew of their foes seventy and five thousand, but they laid not their hands on the prey, 17 On the thirteenth day of the month Adar; and on the fourteenth day of the same rested they, and made it a day of feasting and gladness. 18 But the Jews that were at Shushan assembled together on the thirteenth day thereof, and on the fourteenth thereof; and on the fifteenth day of the same they rested, and made it a day of feasting and gladness. 19 Therefore the Jews of the villages, that dwelt in the unwalled towns, made the fourteenth day of the month Adar a day of gladness and feasting, and a good day, and of sending portions one to another.

9.3.1.en: When the king presented to Esther the number of the slain in Shushan the palace (five hundred men and the ten sons of Haman), she asked him to allow them to kill their enemies on the following day as well, and to hang the sons of Haman on the gallows. Esther did not ask this out of love of bloodshed, but perhaps she realized that the enemy was still devising plans to make Haman's plan succeed, so she wanted to put an end to the matter, while the hanging of Haman's sons was to be a warning to anyone who might be tempted to devise evil.

9.3.2.en: In any case, what Esther did signifies the believer's obligation to strike the works of the devil to the end, leaving no remnant of him inside the palace (the heart), lest the enemy rise again and fight the soul anew. Let us cut off from the palace of our inner life every root of sin, so that the palace may be holy for the Lord.

9.3.3.en: This was with regard to Shushan the palace; but as for all the provinces, they kept to the king's decision that the vengeance should be on the thirteenth day alone, and no other day was given.

9.4.0.en: 20 And Mordecai wrote these things, and sent letters unto all the Jews that were in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, both nigh and far, 21 To stablish this among them, that they should keep the fourteenth day of the month Adar, and the fifteenth day of the same, yearly, 22 As the days wherein the Jews rested from their enemies, and the month which was turned unto them from sorrow to joy, and from mourning into a good day: that they should make them days of feasting and joy, and of sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor. 23 And the Jews undertook to do as they had begun, and as Mordecai had written unto them; 24 Because Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had devised against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast Pur, that is, the lot, to consume them, and to destroy them; 25 But when Esther came before the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked device, which he devised against the Jews, should return upon his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows. 26 Wherefore they called these days Purim after the name of Pur. Therefore for all the words of this letter, and of that which they had seen concerning this matter, and which had come unto them, 27 The Jews ordained, and took upon them, and upon their seed, and upon all such as joined themselves unto them, so as it should not fail, that they would keep these two days according to their writing, and according to their appointed time every year; 28 And that these days should be remembered and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and that these days of Purim should not fail from among the Jews, nor the memorial of them perish from their seed. 29 Then Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew, wrote with all authority, to confirm this second letter of Purim. 30 And he sent the letters unto all the Jews, to the hundred twenty and seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, with words of peace and truth, 31 To confirm these days of Purim in their times appointed, according as Mordecai the Jew and Esther the queen had enjoined them, and as they had decreed for themselves and for their seed, the matters of the fastings and their cry. 32 And the decree of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim; and it was written in the book.

9.4.1.en: Mordecai sent to all the Jews in all the provinces belonging to the kingdom of Persia that they should celebrate on the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month of Adar every year, as a remembrance of the Lord's work with them, and that they should give gifts and donations to the poor. For as the Lord cared for them and saved their lives, each one should care for his neighbor and not ignore the poor and needy... This feast was called the "Feast of Purim". We have already spoken about its ritual.

9.4.2.en: Esther also sent, together with Mordecai, confirming the necessity of celebrating the feast as a hymn of thanksgiving to God, who works on behalf of His children. As St. Jerome says: [Esther, a type of the Church, delivered her people from danger, and having slain Haman, whose name means "injustice", she handed down to the generations a memorial day and a great feast].
